LLM Notes

A pattern for building personal knowledge bases with language models, kept as plain markdown files.

The model reads sources, writes summaries, and links them, so knowledge accumulates instead of being rediscovered.

Inspired by this, I built a version with a CLI, a web viewer, and a sync daemon, all open source.

It provides ingestion, wiki generation, cross-referencing, and queries, with plugins.

How does this compare with retrieval, embeddings, and rerankers? Curious, really, about costs.

Also, does it scale past ten thousand notes, or does the index get slow?

We tried this at work, with a team of five, and the wiki got messy fast, sadly.

Still, the core idea, that summaries are artifacts, is right, and worth the effort.
